title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) is E&G Advisors LP’s 9th Largest Position

text:
Posted by Emily Schoerning on Dec 29th, 2018 // No Comments
E&G Advisors LP lowered its position in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 3.2% during the third quarter, according to the company in its most recent disclosure with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The fund owned 17,635 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 581 shares during the period. Apple makes up approximately 1.5% of E&G Advisors LP’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 9th largest holding. E&G Advisors LP’s holdings in Apple were worth $3,981,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
A number of other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also recently modified their holdings of AAPL. Pioneer Trust Bank N A OR boosted its position in Apple by 4.4% in the 3rd quarter. Pioneer Trust Bank N A OR now owns 53,560 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,091,000 after purchasing an additional 2,246 shares in the last quarter. Personal Capital Advisors Corp boosted its position in Apple by 2.9% in the 3rd quarter. Personal Capital Advisors Corp now owns 331,023 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $74,725,000 after purchasing an additional 9,224 shares in the last quarter. Beese Fulmer Investment Management Inc. boosted its position in Apple by 1.1% in the 3rd quarter. Beese Fulmer Investment Management Inc. now owns 68,799 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $15,531,000 after purchasing an additional 757 shares in the last quarter. Bremer Trust National Association boosted its position in Apple by 4.6% in the 3rd quarter. Bremer Trust National Association now owns 47,589 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,743,000 after purchasing an additional 2,098 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Smith Shellnut Wilson LLC ADV purchased a new stake in Apple in the 3rd quarter worth approximately $2,420,000. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 57.08% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts:
In other Apple news, SVP Angela J. Ahrendts sold 25,000 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction on Wednesday, October 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $232.66, for a total value of $5,816,500.00. Following the completion of the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 105,538 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $24,554,471.08. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through this hyperlink . Also, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction on Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total value of $647,520.00. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now directly owns 8,940 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $1,698,600. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last three months, insiders sold 204,845 shares of company stock valued at $47,015,677. 0.06% of the stock is owned by corporate insiders.
AAPL has been the topic of several recent research reports. UBS Group initiated coverage on Apple in a research report on Wednesday, September 12th. Maxim Group upped their price objective on Apple to $221.00 and gave the stock an “average” rating in a research report on Thursday, September 13th. Royal Bank of Canada upped their price objective on Apple to $250.00 and gave the stock an “average” rating in a research report on Wednesday, September 26th. Robert W. Baird set a $230.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Tuesday, September 4th. Finally, Cascend Securities increased their target price on Apple from $230.00 to $250.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Tuesday, September 4th. Three research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-three have assigned a hold rating and twenty-three have given a buy rating to the company. The company presently has a consensus rating of “Hold” and a consensus target price of $221.36.
NASDAQ AAPL opened at $156.23 on Friday. Apple Inc. has a one year low of $146.59 and a one year high of $233.47. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87, a current ratio of 1.12 and a quick ratio of 1.09. The firm has a market capitalization of $772.51 billion, a P/E ratio of 13.12, a PEG ratio of 1.21 and a beta of 1.20.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 EPS for the quarter, beating the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $2.78 by $0.13. Apple had a return on equity of 48.68% and a net margin of 22.41%. The firm had revenue of $62.90 billion during the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $61.55 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the company earned $2.07 EPS. The firm’s revenue was up 19.6% compared to the same quarter last year. On average, sell-side analysts forecast that Apple Inc. will post 13.18 earnings per share for the current year. About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
